turns.text: Why does Policy Gradient Theorem deserve its own place in the history of artificial intelligence?

Policy-based reinforcement learning needed a rigorous expression for how long-run performance changes with policy parameters. The policy gradient theorem supplied that expression without requiring derivatives of the environment dynamics.

The performance gradient can be written as an expectation of action-value estimates multiplied by the policy score. Actor-critic methods use a learned critic to estimate that value while the actor follows the resulting gradient.

Experts generally treat the policy gradient theorem as the mathematical backbone of modern actor-critic and policy-optimization algorithms. PPO, natural policy gradients, deterministic policy gradients, and many RLHF methods inherit its structure.
As today's systems grow larger, which lessons from Policy Gradient Theorem still matter, and which limits deserve to be questioned again?
